name: browser_storage
description: Inventory a Chromium or Electron LevelDB directory (an IndexedDB, or another LevelDB of a profile: Local Storage, Session Storage) with the pinned ccl_chromium_reader 0.3.18, which this tool runs as a program of its own in the venv of ccl_indexeddb_dump (/opt/dfir/src/ccl_indexeddb_dump/.venv). A survey of what the files hold, not a reading of the browser's state: it says which databases, object stores and keys the records name, where each record is, and shows a bounded preview; it does not say what a page did, when a user acted or which record the browser would return today. A venv that is missing, is not that reader or cannot import it makes the answer status failed with unavailable true, never an empty inventory. WHAT IT READS: the data files NNNNNN.log, NNNNNN.ldb and NNNNNN.sst of the directory, one at a time, each opened without following a link and checked by identity before and after the reader opens it (an entry under a data file's name that is a symbolic link, a FIFO, a device or a directory is refused and named, never opened), and the highest-numbered MANIFEST. A file the reader cannot read to its end is named with its status, the stage and the CLASS of the error (never the message, which can quote evidence), and the records it gave before it stopped are kept; the other files are still read. The reader does not verify the CRC32C of a log record or of a table block, and neither does this tool: a record changed in place is read as it now is. The reader also reads past some damage without an error (measured: a log record cut inside its data, a spanning record that never ends, a length that runs past its batch), so the reader's iteration of log files and table blocks is run with the format's own rules applied: the first inconsistency stops that file (status partial, with the problem named from a fixed list and its offset), a write batch is counted whole or not at all, and a table block compressed in a way other than none or snappy (type 2) is named and not read. A directory whose records include the IndexedDB global-metadata keys is read as an IndexedDB: databases (id, name, origin, the highest object store id), the schema version (read by this tool from the metadata record, because the reader's own field is never filled), and per object store the data records by state (put, delete), the distinct keys, current_keys (the key's newest record, by sequence number, is a put), deleted_keys (it is a delete), the key types and the counts of exists, index and blob entries. Any other directory is a plain LevelDB: counts only, with a preview of the first records, and Local Storage and Session Storage records are NOT interpreted. A store whose metadata record is missing is listed with has_metadata false. WHAT A RECORD SAYS: put and delete are the states the files record at a sequence number; a record is located by its file, its offset (the start of the record in a log file or an uncompressed table block, the start of its block in a compressed one: offset_is says which), its sequence number and its state. A JavaScript Date is shown as ISO 8601 UTC with milliseconds; its raw bytes are in the record's raw_b64 in the values file. The reader's decoding of a negative 32-bit integer is one too high (it reads -1 as 0); this tool decodes that tag as V8 defines it. The decoding of V8 and Blink values is the reader's and is not checked here beyond the cases the tool's tests cover; a value the reader cannot decode is counted by the class of its error (records_not_decoded), and a value the browser moved to a blob file is counted the same way, since no blob directory is read. PREVIEWS: preview_records (default 3, at most 25) records of each store (the first current records, in file order), the key and the value after the shared withholding, bounded in depth (4), in entries a level (12) and in preview_chars characters a text. A name, a key or a text shaped like a token, user-info or a credential is replaced by a marker, and a field whose name says it holds a secret is not read at all. WITHHOLDING IS BY SHAPE: a secret of another shape (a plain password, a pronounceable passphrase, a short id) is printed, and a message or cookie store holds such values: a preview is a lead, and a store whose secrets matter is read in a secret_output job. Measured on 1,000 random plants of each shape in preview slots (the Wilson upper bound at 95% in brackets): AWS key ids, JWTs, PEM keys, Password= and password: pairs, ghp_ tokens and 40-digit hex strings: none printed (at most 0.4% each); a random base64 text of 16 bytes: 15.3% printed (17.7%), of 20 bytes 17.4% (19.9%), of 32 bytes 1.2% (2.1%); user-info whose password holds an @: 3.3% (4.6%); a key id split by NUL characters 8.1% (10.0%), by zero-width spaces 6.7% (8.4%), and a token in UTF-16 text read as one-byte 4.0% (5.4%). NUL and zero-width characters are removed from a printed text. TRIED: against ccl_chromium_reader 0.3.18 with Brotli 1.2.1, zstd 1.5.7.2 and ccl_simplesnappy 0.4, on Python 3.12 and amd64 only; not on arm64 and not on the images' Python 3.11. VALUES TO A FILE: write_values true (only in a job run as secret output: the manifest's secret_output makes every job of this tool that sets it one, and the tool refuses a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1; refused as JSON outside a job, before anything is opened or made) writes EVERY data record of the selected stores (db_id, store_id; all by default), puts and deletes, to browser-storage-records.jsonl under $OUT, mode 0600, created exclusively and never through a link (a second export in one job is refused): a header line, one line per record (n, locator, database, store, names, key, key_type, key_raw_b64, the decoded value or its error class, raw_b64 = the record's value bytes whole) and an end line with the count, so a file cut short is recognisable. The answer then carries counts, the store inventory and the file's name, size and line count read back from the kept file, and no preview and no value. A record value over 48 MiB is named without its bytes (records_over_the_line_limit) and the status is partial; the file stops at 1 GiB. BOUNDS: more than 256 MiB of data files or more than 5,000 is refused before anything is read (the reader holds every record in memory); the reading stops at 2,000,000 records; the reader's process has a 3 GiB address-space limit where the system enforces one (Linux); max_seconds (default 90, at most 100) is the reader's own clock, and a run that reaches it answers with what it had (status partial, stopped deadline). The listing is bounded at 200 databases and 200 stores each (status partial, select with db_id and store_id). A directory without a data file is unsupported. STATUS: complete only when every data file was read to its end, nothing under a data file's name was refused, no limit or clock stopped the reading, the IndexedDB metadata (when present) and the MANIFEST were read, and a values file (when asked for) is whole with its end line; partial otherwise; failed when the reader could not run or no data file could be read. Exit code 0 is complete. The reader's standard error is discarded. SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end the reader and what it started and give one JSON answer (partial, interrupted true), exit 128 plus the signal.

path.description: The LevelDB directory: an origin's *.indexeddb.leveldb directory, or a Local Storage or Session Storage 'leveldb' directory. A symbolic link is refused.

preview_records.description: Records previewed per object store (default 3, 0 to 25; 0 shows none). Ignored with write_values, which previews nothing.

preview_chars.description: Characters of one text in a preview, after the withholding (default 64, 8 to 200).

db_id.description: Only the object stores of this IndexedDB database id are previewed or written (the inventory lists all).

store_id.description: Only the object store with this id is previewed or written.

write_values.description: Write every selected data record whole to a 0600 file under $OUT (a job run as secret output, which the manifest makes of a job that sets this; refused as JSON outside a job and in a job whose process lacks SECRET_OUTPUT=1, before anything is made). The answer carries counts and locators of stores, never a value. Default false.

max_seconds.description: The reader's own clock in seconds (default 90, 5 to 100); a run that reaches it is partial and says so.
